newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief relieved at end of Peru hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief relieved at end of Peru hostage crisis.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Wednesday said he was relieved that the Peru hostage drama had ended with the safe rescue of nearly all the captives.
In a statement, he said he applauded "the determined efforts made by the government of Peru over the past several months to find a negotiated solution."
But he said he regretted "that these efforts were not successful and that it was found necessary, in the end, to resort to force in order to bring this deplorable act of terrorism to a close."
The Security Council's current president, Antonio Monteiro of Portugal, said the 15-seat council "reiterated its strong condemnation of all forms of terrorism."

Peruvian troops stormed the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima in a surprise assault on Tuesday and rescued 71 of the 72 hostages. One hostage, two commandos and all 14 rebels who had held the captives since Dec. 17 were killed.
